audit_items.proof_trace: The code only checks if zero blobs are returned (line 684) but does not validate that len(blobAndProofV2s) equals len(versionedHashes). When the execution layer returns M < N blobs (where N = number of KZG commitments), the pre-allocated array from GetBlobsV2 contains M filled elements and N-M nil elements, but only the M elements are iterated. This allows partial blob sets to pass validation, violating the invariant that ALL blobs must be retrieved before publishing.
audit_items.attack_scenario: A malicious execution layer receives a request for N KZG commitments but returns only M < N blobs (with M > 0 to bypass the zero-check at line 684). Prysm accepts the incomplete response, processes only M blobs, and proceeds with data column construction using an incomplete blob set, causing the node to publish invalid data columns with missing blobs.
